uw.quote: Twin Barges, Seychelles Small wreck lying at 16m. Plenty of macro life and very nice reef system adjacent to it.

highlights.text: Macro life and an adjacent reef

uw.quote: Aquarium, Beau Vallon., Seychelles Diverse reef fish, nudi's, sea slugs, turtles, scorpionfish, stonefish, water temperate around 25-26 C, none to very mild current, perfect for novice divers and above.

km.quote: Aquarium sits just off the northern tip of Mahé near Beau Vallon, at depths between 5 and 18 metres, with minimal current and good visibility on calm days.

summary.text: A sheltered, fish-rich reef off Beau Vallon on Mahé's north tip with little or no current. It is the usual first dive for newly certified divers, with nudibranchs, turtles and scorpionfish among the rocks.

km.quote: Bay Ternay Marine Park diving is the standout inshore option for intermediate divers. … Permit fees apply and are collected through your dive operator … The sites within the park run 8 to 22 metres, with nurse sharks under ledges being the reliable highlight. Visibility averages 12 to 18 metres.

access.value: Marine park permit fee, paid through the dive operator

km.quote: L'ilot, a small islet off the northeast coast, offers slightly more topographic interest — granite boulders at 12 to 20 metres with resident moray eels, lionfish, and occasional turtle sightings. Current here is mild to moderate depending on tide

sm.quote: rocky formations that are home to large reef fish and formations of soft coral. From November to March, you may even get luck and encounter a whale shark.

highlights.text: Granite boulders with morays and lionfish

km.quote: Lighthouse Rock, closer to Mahé's southern tip, is an intermediate site that gets overlooked in favour of the more marketed northern sites. Depths run 12 to 25 metres, current is moderate

sm.quote: Shark Bank is a huge rock that is located 8 km north-west of Mahé, extending down into the ocean depths. … The diversity on show here is something at which to marvel, between 18 metres and 30 metres deep.

km.quote: Shark Bank sits approximately 8 kilometres west of Mahé, rising from around 40 metres to a shallowest point of 18 metres. Current here ranges from negligible to genuinely punishing

highlights.text: Snapper, jack and batfish schools; reef sharks

summary.text: An offshore granite seamount about 8 km from Mahé, rising from deep water to roughly 18 m. Big schools, turtles and reef sharks gather around boulders and arches; currents range from glassy to strong, so it suits advanced divers.

sm.quote: The Aldebaran is a 28 metres fishing boat that sunk in 2008. These days, it attracts colourful marine life, including small fish, moray eels, lionfish, sweetlips, starfish, and batfish. … The wreck is located about 28 - 40 metres deep into the water, where the currents can be strong.

km.quote: it's a 40-minute boat ride minimum, it's exposed to southwest swell during the Southeast Monsoon … When conditions allow, the granite formations around Conception Rocks drop to 30 metres … Hawksbill turtles here are so common

hazards.text: Exposed to swell in the Southeast Monsoon

access.value: Long boat ride (40+ min); not run by all operators

sm.quote: Brissare Rocks , which you can visit from September to May. Due to strong currents, the area attracts different big fish, including smaller sharks and barracudas. The colourful coral arrays bring with them an impressive collection of fish down to a maximum depth of 20 metres.

sp.quote: Ave Maria is a small island located between Praslin and the Sister Island Atoll. Here, divers can achieve a maximum depth of about 20 metres. … Reef sharks, stingrays, batfish, lobsters, and octopuses can be seen here, along with barracuda.

kp.quote: Ave Maria: 15–22 metres, intermediate, visibility 18–28 metres. The best visibility in the Praslin dive site network, consistently.

summary.text: A rocky islet between Praslin and the Sister Islands with granite arches and deeper boulders, reaching about 20 m. Reef sharks, rays and lobsters are regular, and visibility is among the best on the inner islands.

sp.quote: Here you can see beautiful, lush shoals at depths of up to 12 metres. The small island of St. Pierre is a great diving & snorkelling point.

kp.quote: St. Pierre: 10–25 metres, intermediate to advanced depending on tidal phase, visibility 15–25 metres in the inter-monsoon windows. Not suitable for beginners when the current is running.

hazards.text: Not for beginners when current runs
